epithet: One religion, from Nūḥ to Muḥammad ﷺ
lede: The surah that names the line: what was enjoined on Nūḥ, revealed to Muḥammad, and enjoined on Ibrāhīm, Mūsā and ʿĪsā is a single religion. It holds the Qurʾan’s shortest and most decisive statement about Allah — “There is nothing like Him” — and gives a community of believers the rule it is named for.

names.name: al-Shūrā
names.note: From its thirty-eighth ayah, which describes the believers as those “whose affair is consultation among themselves”.

names.name: Ḥā Mīm ʿAyn Sīn Qāf
names.note: It is the only surah whose opening letters fall in two ayat. Ibn al-Jawzī heads it with them.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrimah, Mujāhid, Qatādah and the majority. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah that four of its ayat, beginning with the twenty-third, came down in Madinah, and Muqātil named a few others. It is the third of the Ḥawāmīm; the traditional order places it sixty-second.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ حَم عسق واسْمُها سُورَةُ الشُّورى وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ، رَواهُ العَوْفِيُّ وغَيْرُهُ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وبِهِ قالَ الحَسَنُ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، ومُجاهِدٌ، وقَتادَةُ، والجُمْهُورُ
سُورَةُ الشُّورَى مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْحَسَنِ وَعِكْرِمَةَ وَعَطَاءٍ وَجَابِرٍ. وَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ وَقَتَادَةُ: إِلَّا أَرْبَعَ آيَاتٍ مِنْهَا أُنْزِلَتْ بِالْمَدِينَةِ

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ ﴿حم﴾ ﴿عسق﴾ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn Mardawayh.

attested.quote: ورُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وقَتادَةَ أنَّها مَكِّيَّةٌ إلّا أرْبَعَ آياتٍ مِنها أُنْزِلَتْ بِالمَدِينَةِ
attested.says: It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah that it is Makkan, except four ayat that came down in Madinah.

setting: Quraysh treated what Muḥammad ﷺ brought as an innovation — a new religion with which he had broken from his fathers. This surah’s reply is that it is the oldest thing there is. “Thus does He reveal to you, and to those before you.” And then: “He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined on Nūḥ, and what We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined on Ibrāhīm, Mūsā and ʿĪsā: establish the religion, and do not be divided in it.” Those are the five messengers of firm resolve, and their message is one.

If so, why are there so many religions? The surah answers that too: “They did not divide until after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves.” And it gives the Prophet ﷺ his stance in the face of that division, in an ayah that the scholars note holds ten separate instructions: so to this, call; stand firm as you are commanded; do not follow their desires; and say, “I believe in whatever Book Allah has sent down, and I am commanded to do justice among you.”

Its twenty-third ayah was misread early, and Ibn ʿAbbās corrected it. “Say: I ask of you no reward for it, except affection through kinship.” Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said it meant the kin of Muḥammad ﷺ. Ibn ʿAbbās said: you have been hasty. There was no clan of Quraysh in which the Prophet ﷺ did not have kinship — and what he said to them was: I ask nothing of you, only that you respect the ties of kinship between me and you.

In its second half the surah turns from the message to those who accept it, and describes them in a list that became a charter: they rely on their Lord; they avoid the great sins; when they are angry, they forgive; they answer their Lord and keep up the prayer; their affair is decided by consultation among them; they spend of what they have been given; and when they are wronged, they defend themselves — though whoever pardons and makes peace, his reward is with Allah.

occasions.title: “Affection through kinship”
occasions.text: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about “except affection through kinship”. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: “The kin of the family of Muḥammad ﷺ.” Ibn ʿAbbās said: “You have been hasty. There was no branch of Quraysh in which the Prophet ﷺ did not have kinship. He said: only that you keep the tie of kinship that is between me and you.”

aim: To set out the reality of revelation and of the message of Muḥammad ﷺ — that it continues the revelation given to the prophets.
themes: The one religion of the messengers
How Allah speaks to a human being

outline.title: Thus He reveals
outline.summary: Ḥā Mīm. ʿAyn Sīn Qāf. Thus does Allah, the Almighty, the Wise, reveal to you and to those before you. The heavens almost break apart from above them, and the angels glorify their Lord with praise and ask forgiveness for those on earth. We have revealed to you an Arabic Qurʾan, that you may warn the Mother of Towns and those around it, and warn of the Day of Gathering.

outline.title: There is nothing like Him
outline.summary: Whatever you differ over, its judgement is with Allah. The Originator of the heavens and the earth: He made for you mates from yourselves. There is nothing like Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing (42:11). His are the keys of the heavens and the earth.

outline.title: The same religion
outline.summary: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined on Nūḥ, and what We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined on Ibrāhīm, Mūsā and ʿĪsā: establish the religion and do not divide in it. They divided only after knowledge had come to them. So to that, call; stand firm as you are commanded; and say: “I believe in whatever Book Allah has sent down.” It is Allah who sent down the Book with truth, and the Balance.

outline.title: The harvest of each
outline.summary: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase his harvest; whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him of it, and he has no share in the Hereafter. Or have they partners who have laid down for them a religion Allah did not permit? Say: I ask of you no reward for it, only affection through kinship. It is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds. It is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired.

outline.title: The believers described
outline.summary: Whatever misfortune strikes you is for what your hands have earned — and He pardons much. What you have been given is the enjoyment of this life; what is with Allah is better and more lasting, for those who believe and rely on their Lord: who avoid the great sins, and forgive when they are angry; who answer their Lord and establish the prayer, whose affair is consultation among themselves, and who spend of what We have provided. The recompense of an ill deed is one like it; but whoever pardons and makes peace, his reward is with Allah. And whoever is patient and forgives — that is of the matters requiring resolve.

outline.title: Before a Day that cannot be turned back
outline.summary: You will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying: “Is there any way of return?” Answer your Lord before there comes from Allah a Day that cannot be averted. If they turn away, We have not sent you as their keeper; yours is only to convey. To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth: He grants females to whom He wills and males to whom He wills, or both, and makes whom He wills barren.

outline.title: How Allah speaks to a human being
outline.summary: It is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger to reveal by His leave what He wills. Thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith; but We have made it a light by which We guide whom We will. And you guide to a straight path — the path of Allah.

keyAyah.why: The rule for everything said about Allah: nothing is like Him — and in the same breath, He hears and He sees. It denies likeness and affirms the attributes together.

before: Fuṣṣilat spoke of the Book and those who turned from it. Al-Shūrā speaks of the revelation itself, and places it in the line of every revelation before it.
after: Al-Shūrā ends: you did not know what the Book was. Al-Zukhruf opens by swearing by that Book, and saying where it is kept: in the Mother of the Book, with Us.
